Data Collection and Distribution Area â This application acts as an MI repository for current applications and active loan information. It is fed daily by data feeds from CIA, PAD, Appscore, ASM and Pancredit. Every time an activity occurs on an active loan on Pancredit during a working day, that data is passed into DCDA on an overnight batch and from DCDA data is passed to various downstream systems like Lemans, GDW, Hadoop, COBRA, National Sales etc. It is also used as the source of information for some loan enquiry APIs. Every loan application through CIA and PAD is captured in DCDA even if it never gets as far as being an activated loan, this information is also passed into DCDA via overnight batch and ahead of the Pancredit update, as an application from CIA/PAD may have completed during the same day and the new account details would then also be provided by Pancredit.

As part of the Groupâs ongoing sustainability and environmental responsibility, we have ingested an external data-source, BEIS (Department for Business, Energy & Industrial Strategy) â now called DESNZ (Department for Energy, Security & Net Zero). BEIS contains the latest estimate of UK greenhouse gas emissions since 1990. Two files are published and downloaded at the end of March every year. The files are split into emissions by source (Scope 1 emissions) and emissions by end users (Scope 2 emissions). Within these files, the emissions are broken into high level Sectors (e.g. Buildings and product uses), Subsectors (e.g. Commercial buildings) and Categories (e.g. Commercial combustion).Â 

The current user of the data (Portfolio Analytics) uses the BEIS data (along with data from ONS (Office for National Statistics)) to calculate emissions factors in case they are unable to obtain any higher quality data.

This ingestion is a strategic initiative aimed at enhancing our Net Zero reporting solution. It continues the work required to create an automated, strategic solution, reduce the reliance on the tactical, manual solution and will lead to data accuracy improvements for reporting. Landing this data into GCP, as an ODP, ensures that the data will be reusable and extensible across the wider group as part of a Foundation Data Products (i.e. Economic Activity Emissions Value and Economic Activity Valuation FDPs â already come through DP governance).

As part of the Groupâs ongoing sustainability and environmental responsibility, we have ingested an external data-source, PCAF (Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials), which contains emission factors. that enable financial institutions to calculate their footprint in line with the PCAF Standards. For each data quality score and asset class, the appropriate, publicly available data sources have been analysed and verified, from which emission factors are derived by PCAF. By focusing on providing physical- and economic-activity based emission factors, financial institutions can start using the PCAF Database, even with limited data availability on reported emissions from the borrower or investee. The data is downloaded from the PCAF company website every time is updated which is currently twice a year (end of March and September).Â 

Emission Factors help in estimating the environmental impact of various activities by providing a standardized measure of emissions per unit of activity. To calculate GHG emissions, you can multiply the activity data by the emission factor. When we donât have the emissions data for a company, we use the emission factors from PCAF, specifically tailored for the industrial sector and classification. For example, if we couldnât get the emissions for a dairy farm from a trusted source, then we would use the value from PCAF for dairy farms that would give it in tCO2e/M. Euro, then would multiply the amount by the denominator/unit of activity.Â

A data product that contains measurements of emissions (both mass and intensity) related to industry sector emissions (economic activity).

The data product standardises sources for this data and where new industry sector emission sources are identified, should be extended to include these.

The standardisation is achieved by holding the common attributes of industry sector emissions (emission scope, region, measurement unit and classification as reference data) in reference tables. The emission values from multiple sources are stored in a table within the data product called "economic_activity_emission_value" which links to the reference tables to achieve standardisation.

Please refer to the Group Data Model concept, "Environmental Social Governance". Within this the data product is described under "Emission".

Industry sector emission

A data product that contains measurements of UK economic activity valuation data.

The data product standardises sources for this data and where new UK economic activity valuation sources are identified, should be extended to include these.

The standardisation is achieved by holding the common attributes of UK economic activity valuation data (measurement, asset type and publisher) as reference data in reference tables. The emission values from multiple sources are stored in tables within the data product called "economic_activity_value" and "economic_activity_capital_stock" which links to the reference tables to achieve standardisation.

LBG is a founding member of the UN-convened Net-Zero Banking Alliance. Members of the Alliance (who represent circa 40% of global banking assets) are committed to aligning their lending and investment portfolios toward achieving net-zero emissions by 2050.
